title: Get Ahead of Norway's eInvoicing Mandate with SAP Business Network for Procurement
author: yogesh-sap
text:
Norway's eInvoicing Mandate: Why SAP Business Network Users Are Already Ahead 
 Norway is introducing mandatory B2B eInvoicing from 1 January 2027. If your business is already transacting on SAP Business Network for Procurement, the good news is straightforward: you are already compliant, with no additional configuration steps required. 
 The Mandate: What Norway Requires 
 From 1 January 2027, all bookkeeping-obligated businesses in Norway must issue electronic invoices for domestic B2B transactions. A second phase in January 2030 will extend the obligation to the mandatory receiving and processing of eInvoices, aligned with Norway's Digital Bookkeeping Act and the broader European VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) initiative. 
 The mandate requires invoices to be structured, standardized, and machine-readable. Businesses must also register in ELMA, Norway's electronic address registry, comply with SAF-T reporting requirements, and archive invoices for a minimum of five years. Exemptions apply for entities with annual turnover below NOK 50,000 and certain financial institutions. 
 An important clarification: the use of the Peppol network is not mandated for all businesses. The regulation focuses on the format and structure of invoices, not on a single mandatory transport network. This means businesses have flexibility in how they exchange compliant eInvoices with their trading partners. 
 Already on SAP Business Network? You Are Ready. 
 For buyers and suppliers already transacting on SAP Business Network for Procurement, the path to compliance is not a project. It is business as usual. 
 SAP Business Network delivers regulatory consistent invoicing today. The platform already supports the structured, standardized invoice formats required under Norwegian law, with country-specific business rules applied automatically to every transaction. No additional configuration steps are needed for existing SAP Business Network users to meet the mandate's issuance requirements. 
 This is a significant advantage for businesses that have already invested in digitizing their procurement and invoicing processes through SAP Business Network. While others are scrambling to find a compliant eInvoicing solution before the 2027 deadline, SAP Business Network customers can approach the mandate with confidence. 
 Outbound Invoicing: The Core of Compliance 
 The primary story for Norway compliance on SAP Business Network is outbound invoicing - the process by which suppliers issue regulatory compliant invoices directly on the network. 
 Suppliers on SAP Business Network continue to use the familiar purchase order flip process, exactly as they do today. Norway-specific country rules and the business rules configured by the buyer are applied automatically during invoice creation, validating the invoice before it reaches the buyer. The result is a pre-validated, compliant invoice delivered directly into the buyer's ERP backend, whether SAP S/4HANA, SAP ECC, or Ariba Buying and Invoicing, ready for posting with minimal manual intervention. 
 This pre-validation step is a meaningful operational benefit beyond compliance: fewer rejections, faster processing, and higher auto-posting rates that reduce cost and effort for both buyers and suppliers. 
 Inbound Invoicing: A Bridge for Non-Network Suppliers 
 Not every supplier is on SAP Business Network. For buyers who need to receive compliant eInvoices from suppliers transacting outside the network, SAP Business Network offers an inbound invoicing capability that acts as a bridge. 
 Through its integration with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance (DRC) Cloud Edition, SAP Business Network can receive invoices submitted by suppliers via the Peppol network, in EHF 3.0 or Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 format, and deliver them into the buyer's backend system for reconciliation and posting. Suppliers using this route do not need a SAP Business Network account; they simply exchange invoices via their own chosen Peppol access point. 
 This inbound capability extends compliance coverage to the full supplier base, ensuring that even suppliers not yet on SAP Business Network can deliver invoices that meet Norway's regulatory requirements. 
 One Platform, Consistent Compliance 
 Norway's mandate is part of a broader wave of eInvoicing regulation sweeping across Europe and beyond. SAP Business Network for Procurement is built for exactly this environment, providing regulatory consistent invoicing across more than 40 countries from a single platform. 
 For businesses already on SAP Business Network, Norway is not a compliance challenge. It is a confirmation that the investment in a modern, connected procurement network was the right one. 
 To learn more about how SAP Business Network supports eInvoicing compliance in Norway and globally, visit Business Network page or speak with your SAP account team.

title: Hands-on Tutorial: Improve your time-series forecasts with SAP's Tabular AI model SAP-RPT-TS
author: AndreasForster
text:
Tabular AI is causing a big stir in the world of traditional Machine Learning. Since Tabular AI models are pre-trained , there is no need anymore to train, tune and maintain a specific Machine Learning model for each task. 
 This makes forecasting on structured data accessible to non-Data Scientists. And Data Scientists have a good chance to get more accurate predictions with less effort, compared to traditional Machine Learning (a.k.a. Narrow AI). What’s not to like? Win-win for everyone! 
 On top of its existing models from the RPT and TabPFN family, SAP has just released SAP-RPT-TS ., a Foundation Model specifically for time-series forecasting. Time-series forecasting is by far the most common requirement that I am seeing on tabular data. So I ran a few tests and comparisons, and I am impressed by the results! 
 This blog guides you through making your own SAP-RPT-TS forecasts through SAP AI Core. For a quick test you can also try your own data in the RPT Playground . If you have a SAP HANA Cloud instance, you can also get SAP-RPT-TS forecasts through SQL/Python , without needing to extract or move any data.

title: SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment – Maintenance Windows and Major Upgrade Windows in 2027
author: AndreasWehry
text:
One of the benefits of using SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment (also known as "Steampunk") is that updates and upgrades are applied by SAP to the systems in quite a high frequency and close to the corresponding release time. 
 Find the latest known schedule of Major Upgrade Windows and Weekly Maintenance Windows for 2027 in this blog post. 
 Major Upgrade Windows 
 As in 2026 , the SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment will have 4 Major Upgrade Windows in 2027 . These 24 hours of potential system unavailability are used to upgrade the systems to the next major version. 
 The events for the Major Upgrade Windows are harmonized between all SAP Cloud Products and scheduled for the following weekends: 
 February 12th – 14th (Release 2702) 
 May 14th – 16th (Release 2705) 
 August 13th – 15th (Release 2708) 
 November 12rd – 14th (Release 2711) 
 Depending on the data center region, the 24 hours downtime will start/end at: 
 MENA: FRI 1 am - SAT 1 am UTC 
 APJ: FRI 9 pm – SAT 9 pm UTC 
 Europe: SAT 4 am – SUN 4 am UTC 
 Americas: SAT 10 am – SUN 10 am UTC 
 Please find the release schedule of the referenced UI5 versions in this blog post . 
 Weekly/Monthly Maintenance Windows 
 Potentially every weekend, the SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment could use a downtime of 4 hours, to apply SAP HANA Cloud updates, Hotfix Collections and other changes. 
 Depending on the data center region, the 4 hours downtime may start at: 
 MENA: FRI 5 pm UTC 
 APJ: SAT 1 pm UTC 
 Europe: SAT 8 pm UTC 
 Americas: SUN 2 am UTC 
 The events for the release 2702 are planned as Weekly Maintenance Windows in 2027. Please note that the frequency of the HFC import is adjusted to monthly to align with the S/4 delivery cycle. As soon as the specific dates are known, they will be posted here: 
 The following events for the release 2611 are planned in 2026/2027. Systems are supplied with hotfix collections (HFC) once a month. In the intervals between these HFC updates, there are now lifecycle events so-called Emergency Patch deployments (EP deployments) without a downtime: 
 Hotfix Collection 3 for Release 2611 (only for systems which belong to the pre-upgrade) | November 13th, 2026 
 EP Deployment (HFC 3) for Release 2611 | November 30th, 2026 
 Hotfix Collection 4 for Release 2611 | December 4th – 6th, 2026 
 EP Deployment (HFC 4) for Release 2611 | December 20th, 2026 
 Hotfix collection 5 for Release 2611 | January 1st - 3rd, 2027 
 EP Deployment (HFC 5) for Release 2611 | January 17th, 2027 
 Actually Required Technical Downtime 
 The maintenance windows described above refer to the contractual SLAs. The actual technical downtime required is significantly lower. We introduced Downtime-optimized Upgrades and Hotfix Collection Imports for Production . Please take into consideration, that only non-development systems will benefit from the downtime-optimized upgrades and hotfix collection imports. As explained in the above-mentioned blog post, you can adjust the begin of the technical downtime of those systems within a 4 hours timeframe. 
 Cloud System Notification Subscriptions (CSNS) 
 Please register to Cloud System Notification Subscriptions (CSNS) in SAP for Me to get important information about planned and unplanned downtimes: 
 Access to Cloud System Notification Subscriptions (CSNS): https://me.sap.com/systemsprovisioning/getNotified 
 Find more information about Cloud System Notification Subscriptions (CSNS) in this documentation 
 To find the SAP Business AI Platform, ABAP environment entry select: 
 Cloud Service: SAP BTP, ABAP environment 
 Solution Area: SAP Build 
 References 
 Maintenance Windows and Major Upgrade Windows for SAP Cloud Services 
 SAP Note 2888562 – Intelligent Enterprise Suite: Harmonized release calendar for SAP Cloud products 
 Service Level Agreement for SAP Cloud Services

title: Winston Chat for SAP SuccessFactors – How are Hire Transactions counted for licensing?
author: barbara_gentner8286fb
text:
Hello SAP Community, 
 I'm looking for clarification on the licensing model for SmartRecruiters Winston Chat for SAP SuccessFactors. 
 As I understand it, Winston Chat is licensed based on annual Hire Transactions, sold in blocks of 100, with a minimum commitment of 500 transactions. 
 However, I'm struggling to find a clear definition of how these transactions are counted in practice.

 Are internal hires or internal transfers counted in the same way as external hires?

title: SAP Positioned as a Market Shaper in the Inaugural 2026 Gartner® Emerging Market Quadrant for Integrated Supply Chain AI Agents – Established Vendors
author: Devesh Mishra
text:
The supply chain AI conversation is shifting. For years, the focus was on faster insights, better forecasts, and sharper visibility. That era delivered value, but it also revealed a gap: knowing what is happening is not the same as acting on it. 
 Accelerate outcomes with context-aware agents and assistants that know your work and your business 

 Learn how 

 AI agents are now creating a new chapter. The next frontier is no longer analyzing faster, but letting agents act: working together across planning, procurement, manufacturing, logistics, and operations. 

 For more than 50 years, SAP has helped organizations run their supply chains by connecting business context, intelligence, and execution across end-to-end processes. 

 We are proud to share that SAP has been positioned in the Market Shapers quadrant of the inaugural Gartner® Emerging Market Quadrant for Integrated Supply Chain AI Agents – Established Vendors . This is Gartner’s first formal assessment of this emerging category. In our view, it reflects the progress we have made in bringing AI agents into the heart of supply chain operations, and the direction we continue to take. 

 Gartner describes the Market Shapers quadrant this way: 

 “Vendors in this quadrant are defined by advanced multiagent solutions available across supply chain functions for greater operational impact. Moving beyond assistive solutions or siloed automation, these agents are able to reason across functions and systems, sense and respond to shifts in data, and execute autonomously, sometimes interacting with other agents or systems inside the enterprise, to solve more complex goals. These solutions are further elevated by optimization techniques such as decision modeling, knowledge graphs, digital twins, and ontology layers to improve agent performance.” 

 From assistants to orchestrated agents 

 Supply chain decisions never happen in isolation. A supplier delay can ripple through production schedules, logistics, customer commitments, and financial results. Yet much of the AI in supply chains today still works within a single function or a single task. It can point out a problem, but people still must weigh the trade-offs and act across several systems. 

 With Autonomous Supply Chain Management , people define goals and priorities, AI assistants orchestrate activity across domains, and agents execute the work within governed, end-to-end processes. Through Joule , role-specific assistants coordinate specialized AI agents across design, planning, sourcing, manufacturing, delivery, and operations. Together, they sense disruptions, analyze the impact, simulate alternatives, and execute coordinated responses, with people making the decisions that matter most. 

 Joule is where it all comes together. People express what they want to achieve, and Joule Assistants take it from there. Each assistant is tailored to a specific role, while agents handle specialized tasks within business-defined guardrails. 

 For example, when a planner describes a goal, the Supply Chain Planning Assistant coordinates demand, inventory, and capacity agents to build and simulate scenarios, so the planner can focus on evaluating outcomes and making the decision. People direct. Assistants coordinate. Agents execute. 

 And because SAP supply chain agents work within the broader SAP Autonomous Suite, a supply chain decision can trigger the right financial, workforce, or customer action as part of the same coordinated response. 

 Agents that act where the work happens 

 We believe AI agents create real value only when they move from recommendation to execution safely. Greater autonomy must be accompanied by greater accountability. As agents take on more responsibility, organizations need visibility into what those agents are doing and why. That requires three things working together. 

 First, agents need to work inside the system of record. SAP agents operate directly in SAP Cloud ERP and the SAP supply chain management suite executing production orders, convert requisitions, or direct warehouse tasks, with no middleware between decision and action. They can also extend coordination to trading partners through SAP Business Network. 

 Second, agents need business context. SAP Business Data Cloud, SAP Knowledge Graph, and our supply chain semantic model give agents a shared understanding of business entities, relationships, and rules. That helps them understand what a signal means across domains and how a disruption will affect the business. 

 Third, agents need governance. Through SAP Business AI Platform, Joule Studio lets customers and partners build agents, and SAP AI Agent Hub governs both SAP and non-SAP agents with identity enforcement, audit trails, and explainability. Joule Work gives people one place to monitor and act on agent recommendations. 

 Delivering real results for customers 

 Customers will not value us by how many agents we build, but by the outcomes those agents deliver. Recognition is only meaningful when it reflects real impact for our customers, that are already putting supply chain agents to work with capabilities available today. 

 Takeda Pharmaceuticals will use Industry AI for regulated manufacturing, where agents monitor production KPIs, flag deviations, and initiate corrective workflows in GxP environments. The expected results include up to 10% productivity gain and 25% less stock-out revenue loss. 

 Lemvigh-Mueller deployed three coordinated agents to handle supplier order confirmations, reaching more than 90% touchless processing of 100,000 confirmations a year. 

 RWE is applying Autonomous Asset Management to its offshore wind fleet, where AI agents analyze past incidents, identify root causes, and generate pre-filled work orders for technicians. 

 Looking ahead 

 Supply chains don’t become autonomous overnight. The journey happens step by step: starting with agents that recommend, then agents that act within clear guardrails, and expanding autonomy as data, processes, and governance mature. 

 As we work with our customers and partners, our agent coverage will continue to expand every quarter across supply chain domains. 

 We are grateful to our customers, partners, analysts, and SAP teams whose collaboration shapes our products and strategy. We see this recognition as an important milestone, and we remain committed to helping organizations turn their supply chains into a source of resilience and lasting business value. 

 Devesh Mishra, General Manager and Chief Product Officer for SAP Supply Chain Management

title: Business Networks Harness Agentic AI to Bolster Collaboration and Operational Resilience Among Trading Partners
author: Jörn Keller
text:
Enterprises lately are deploying artificial intelligence in a plethora of ingenious ways—everything from tailoring cancer treatment , reducing traffic congestion , and optimizing the power grid to composing hit songs , customizing fragrances , and even perfecting pizza pies . 

 Through a burgeoning array of novel applications, businesses are turning to AI to dramatically expand the value they can create for their customers. Often, such applications involve optimizing internal processes: the data, the workflows, the controls managed inside the four walls of a business. But equally important is the value that AI can help to realize beyond those walls, through collaborative relationships with buyers, suppliers, and other key stakeholders. A firm, after all, is only as successful as its ability to manage spend, suppliers, and risk across its ecosystem. This is why the touchpoints between trading partners—the digital networks through which day-to-day operational and transactional data flow up and down the supply chain—hold immense potential to unlock value as businesses increasingly become Autonomous Enterprises . 

 Business networks form an interdependent system within which buyers, suppliers, procurement organizations, service providers, financial institutions, and AI agents coordinate decisions, foster collaboration, and deter disruption. As the world’s largest business-to-business marketplace, SAP Business Network facilitates over US$8 trillion in commerce annually across more than 940 million transactions as of the 12 months ending the third quarter of 2026. Aided by an expanding set of AI agents, the network can contextualize vast troves of operational data to help carry out desired tasks within strict parameters set by businesses seeking to manage risk, ensure compliance, and extend competitive advantage. If enterprise resource planning solutions can be thought of as an organization’s central nervous system, then cloud-based business networks comprise the connective tissue between enterprises seeking to manage spend, facilitate collaboration, and optimize procurement and invoicing processes. 
 No business does business alone. Connect across companies to build stronger supply chains and deliver on the customer promise. 

 Learn how 

 The vision of SAP Business Network is to become the intelligence and execution layer for commerce between companies, transforming the market from fragmented, point-to-point collaboration toward a connected ecosystem in which buyers, suppliers, logistics providers, and asset operators can anticipate change and coordinate decisions in real time. By combining the trusted business processes of SAP Business Suite with multi-enterprise network data, SAP Business Data Cloud , and Joule , SAP’s AI solution embedded across company systems and extensible across non-company systems, SAP Business Network can enable increasingly intelligent, predictive, and autonomous processes across sourcing, procurement, supplier management, and finance. 

 Some of the greatest opportunity to harness value from cross-enterprise AI solutions lies in managing spend and supply chains. Consider, for example, the complexities and costs involved in order prioritization , where a manufacturer must balance revenue, service levels, inventory, and production constraints across multiple parties in real time. To do so, the business runs simulations to surface recommendations for alternative configurations, sourcing strategies, or distribution scenarios, all in hopes of averting disruption that could affect buyers, suppliers, or end-user customers. 

 Years ago, such efforts might have proved unreliable owing to sheer complexity or, worse, fragmented data. But when paired with trading partners’ synchronous operational data converging through business networks, AI can not only produce actionable recommendations but can carry them out with precision and within specified parameters. It can even prompt crucial questions that businesses may have neglected to consider before previously undetected vulnerabilities have the chance to imperil mission-critical processes. When trading partners achieve end-to-end process transparency via the cloud, the intelligence and insights available to them increase exponentially, as do the efficiencies that result. 

 Yet it bears noting that the capabilities made possible by agentic AI neither replace nor diminish the importance of human involvement. When the C-suite leaders responsible for spend management and supply chain strategy evaluate autonomous solutions, governance emerges consistently as a top priority. To ensure accountability and oversight at every link of the supply chain, a business-to-business platform must offer agentic solutions that operate strictly within an organization’s authorized guardrails and internal controls. For compliance and audit purposes, it must also document the various factors that contribute to shaping each automated transaction. Transparency, after all, breeds trust, which in turn spurs adoption at scale. 

 As automated solutions take on a greater share of tactical tasks and routine processes—such as generating demand forecasts, processing purchase orders, optimizing shipment schedules, streamlining warehouse operations, and the like—strategic judgment remains the undisputed province of supply chain and spend management professionals. Because all of the foregoing types of process data weave their way through business networks, they become the ideal fabric on which to embroider agentic AI capabilities. 

 The age-old problem in supply chain management posed by fragmented data residing on siloed, or even incompatible, systems falls away when core operational data intersects in the cloud at the business network layer. Such networks deliver not only a comprehensive view of the supply chain but also the agentic AI capabilities necessary to avert disruption, mitigate risk, and foster strategic collaboration among trading partners. By relying on operational data both contemporaneous and historical, business networks deliver the context within which enterprises can apply AI solutions reliably to solve many of their toughest operational challenges—and to strengthen their trading relationships for long-term mutual success.

title: SAP and Cohere Empower Regulated Industries to Innovate and Deploy AI Faster
author: Brenda Bown
text:
When you ask AI a business question, the answer appears in seconds. What you don’t see is the path that your data traveled to make that answer possible. 
 EU AI cloud: Secure, compliant AI for Europe 

 Learn more 

 Depending on the underlying architecture of your AI solution, that data can cross multiple applications, vendors, and regions before a response ever reaches you. 

 That data journey matters, especially for organizations in regulated industries who are entrusted with sensitive or regulated data. It is why sovereign capabilities have become critical to keeping data within approved geographic boundaries, limiting who can access it, and supporting compliance with data residency and regulatory requirements. 

 Today, to support customers with specific sovereignty and data residency needs, SAP made Cohere’s agentic AI platform, North, generally available on SAP Business AI Platform. North enables enterprises to securely deploy AI agents and workflow automations at scale within their own infrastructure, without compromising on control or compliance. 

 Video: Cohere North on SAP Business AI Platform 

 North: Cohere’s enterprise-grade AI agent platform 

 North sets the standard for business performance by helping teams automate work and accelerate decisions that drive results, all in one scalable, secure workspace. It enables organizations to create AI agents and workflow automations to streamline operations across finance, sales, HR, IT, and customer support. Use cases include forecasting, CRM management, meeting preparation, IT service automation, and enhanced customer service. 

 Deep customization across models, agents, and workflows ensures North adapts to specific organizational needs while maintaining robust control over deployments. 

 The SAP and Cohere partnership is especially valuable in sovereignty-conscious markets globally where AI adoption needs to align with national expectations of security, privacy, transparency, and accessibility. 

 SAP and Cohere’s North platform: Compliant AI made even easier 

 The combination of SAP Business AI Platform and North can deliver exponential value. SAP can help reduce overhead by hosting, operating, and supporting the solution end to end. Our APIs, solutions, and knowledge sources make it easier for North users to build AI agents grounded in their unique business context, policies, and enterprise data. 

 SAP’s managed delivery model connects North’s AI capabilities to SAP environments, reducing the need for organizations to manage separate infrastructure, operations, support, and commercial relationships. In other words, SAP Business AI Platform transforms North into a managed, enterprise-ready, and sovereign AI service. 

 This partnership expands SAP’s sovereign solutions that can be tailored to customer needs. For customers with the most advanced requirements, SAP Sovereign Cloud offers data, operational, technical, and legal sovereignty. Our sovereign AI offerings include EU AI Cloud and Industrial AI Cloud. 

 For regulated industries and the public sector, this is the foundation for adopting AI while keeping sovereignty, compliance, and business value aligned from day one.
